items.title: [Comment] Offline: China bids to lead in global health

But from the perspective of an emerging superpower, it was not surprising at all. The Chinese Government is ready to assert its claim to positions of global leadership, especially now that the USA has turned its back on multilateralism. In Beijing last week, I sat down with Dr Li to listen to her set out her manifesto. She has four pillars supporting her pitch: a more efficient WHO; a safer world; equitable health systems; and harnessing innovation.

items.title: [Correspondence] Women with obstetric fistula in Somalia deserve better

The report does not meet the rigorous editorial standards that we expect from The Lancet. It does a disservice to vulnerable women who have obstetric fistula in Somalia and beyond.

items.title: Lab leak disease outbreaks: the long, murky history
items.summary: In the heart of Russia, fear of plague is spreading. Unbeknown to the outside world, authorities have quietly commandeered the building where the first case emerged. Rifle wielding guards stand at the entrances. Inside, people are locked in quarantine rooms. There have already been deaths—pneumonic plague. And it came from a laboratory.This was the scene at a Moscow hospital in 1939, according to a handful of recollections written by scientists who lived through it.
